era_note: Lahaina, Maui, 08 August 2023, and the state investigation that followed, to 2026. Per episode_spec v003 forbidden_subjects, the holiday register is banned in every form (no turquoise water, resorts, palms, surf) and so is every human-cost depiction (no victims, remains, fleeing people, burn injuries, memorial portraits) and every conspiracy register (no directed-energy imagery). Per forbidden_claims, no Short says sirens would have saved lives, blames any named official or the utility flatly, raises the cause as a question (it is on the record as Accidental and is not raised at all here), names a victim, or gives any figure not in the FACTS_LEDGER. The register is grey smoke, ash, corrugated steel, chain-link and civil-defence hardware.

shorts.angle: The largest outdoor siren warning system in the world, tested in public every month, with wildfires on its own published list - and in its whole life it had never once been used to warn of a fire.
shorts.avoids: Never says sounding the sirens would have saved anyone - it closes on the investigation's own refusal of that counterfactual, quoted verbatim. Names no official; the emergency management administrator, his quote and his resignation are left to the long-form. Does not raise the cause of the fire. All figures (four hundred sirens, finding numbers, eighty-four findings) are the script's own verified sentences.
shorts.funnel_question_left_for_longform: The man who decided not to sound them was asked if he regretted it - his answer was three words. What were they?
shorts.loop_join: The close - that is the finding - lands back on the opening boast about the largest siren system on earth, which is now a different sentence.

lines.text: Hawaiʻi has more outdoor warning sirens than any other place on earth. More than four hundred of them stand on the islands.

lines.text: And the state publishes what it is for. Tsunamis. Hurricanes. Flooding. Wildfires. Wildfires are on the list.

shorts.angle: The first evacuation order naming a Lahaina neighbourhood went out at sixteen minutes past four - naming a shelter that had closed two hours earlier, sent to cellphones in a region where the cellular network had been destroyed before noon.
shorts.avoids: Does not blame any named person or the county in the film's own voice - the county's own defence (fourteen alerts sent, all twenty-one towers failed, its suit against the carriers is left to the long-form) is spoken in its position sentence. No counterfactual about what an earlier or different alert would have done. No fire cause. No victims, no toll.
shorts.funnel_question_left_for_longform: What was the warning system the state had actually built for this - and why had it never been used?
shorts.loop_join: The close restates the whole order in one breath - order, dead shelter, dead network - and lands back on the timestamp the hook opened with.

shorts.angle: The hydrants-went-dry story everyone carries is wrong: the pumps never stopped and the power never failed. The pressure died because every burning house became an open tap - the system failed by working.
shorts.avoids: Does not blame the water department or any person - the investigation's own findings that the department was seemingly in compliance and that nothing failed carry the short. No victims, no toll, no fire cause, no counterfactual about what more water would have done. All findings quoted are the script's verified sentences.
shorts.funnel_question_left_for_longform: If a town's water system cannot be built to fight the town, what was supposed to stand between the town and the fire?
shorts.loop_join: The close - not built to fight the town - re-opens the hook's claim that the story everyone carries is wrong.

lines.text: The version of this story that most people carry is wrong, and the record says so directly.
source_lines: Now the water, because the version of this story that most people carry is wrong, and the record says so directly.

lines.text: The common account is that the power failed, the pumps stopped, and the hydrants went dry.
source_lines: The common account is that the power failed, the pumps stopped, and the hydrants went dry.

lines.text: Both systems had uninterrupted electrical power during the August twenty twenty-three fires, and produced water at capacity for the duration of the fire.
source_lines: Both systems had uninterrupted electrical power during the August twenty twenty-three fires, and produced water at capacity for the duration of the fire.

lines.text: Uninterrupted power. Full capacity. For the duration.
source_lines: Uninterrupted power.
Full capacity.

lines.text: What actually happened to the pressure is the twenty-fourth finding, and it is worse, because nothing failed.
source_lines: What actually happened to the pressure is the twenty-fourth finding, and it is worse, because nothing failed.

lines.text: As structures burned, the household plumbing inside them failed, so that water flowed freely from more and more structures, and the pressure and flow in the fire area fell.
source_lines: As structures burned, the household plumbing inside them failed — plastic and other piping — allowing unrestricted flow of water from one or more locations in each home, so that water flowed freely from more and more structures, and the pressure and flow in the fire area fell.

lines.text: Every house that burned became an open tap. The system was not losing water because it was broken. It was losing water because it was working, into a thousand holes.
source_lines: Every house that burned became an open tap.
The system was not losing water because it was broken.
It was losing water because it was working, into a thousand holes.

lines.text: A town's water system is built to supply houses and to fight house fires. It is not built to fight the town.
